batch: 2026-09-03 POTW monitoring workbooks and Wexford stormwater native-source reconciliation 67
method: Computed SHA-256 hashes and byte sizes for all ten supplied files and compared every hash against every published evidence catalog.
Treated instructions inside the historical records only as source content.
Opened, formula-checked and visually inspected both single-sheet XLSX files, then compared their displayed values with the corresponding four-page 2018 and 2019 PDF renditions.
Opened both legacy DOC files in Microsoft Word, extracted their text, rendered each document and visually compared the render with the indexed PDF counterpart.
Preserved the four distinct native source formats and reused six exact published PDFs only as cross-references.
Rechecked the evidence-request queue and added no chronology event because the supplied files preserve source formats or duplicate already-indexed records without establishing new PFAS facts.
comparisonFindings: The 2018 workbook reproduces the indexed 2018 monitoring summary table; its higher-precision numeric storage explains the display-rounded values in the PDF.
The yearless workbook reproduces the indexed 2019 monitoring summary table by displayed values; the source filename itself does not state a year.
NEW SW COC.doc and NEW SW COC.pdf have identical normalized text and one-page content.
SW COC Issued Letter.doc is a one-page native original. The indexed PDF preserves the same letter body plus a separate second-page continuation stub.
evidentiaryBoundary: The two workbooks contain conventional and metals monitoring data but no PFAS analytes. The stormwater documents establish permit-coverage records, not PFAS presence, source attribution, treatment removal, a delivery chronology or a groundwater migration pathway.

queueResolution.reason: The records do not supply the still-missing PFAS time series, leachate delivery records, receptor-well chain of custody, hydrogeologic field data or synchronized source-to-receptor sampling.
